correctness.rationale: The smooth positive-curvature hypotheses give full-support normal measure, positive admissible support denominators, and smooth radial roots. Joint convexity follows from the perspective of strictly convex log cosh. Any integrated equality for distinct origins would force identical normalized normal coordinates for opposite normals, hence equal y endpoints by positive width and then either identical origins or y=0. This yields strict interior Minkowski inclusion and strict Brunn-Minkowski root-volume concavity. For symmetric bodies, F(tc,y) is even and has strictly positive second t derivative for every y,c nonzero, giving strictly nested radial bodies. The implicit radial equation has strictly positive derivative D and t second derivative N, so rho_tt=-N/D. The polar volume identity gives the exact negative quadratic Hessian with O(t^4) from analytic parity. Lutwak-Yang-Zhang (2010) supplies the Orlicz definition and the scalar perspective inequality (appropriately credited), and proves an ellipsoid global shape optimization—not the fixed-body recentering rigidity and exact second variation. Zhou-Ye-Zhang (arXiv:2501.07565) develops higher-order Orlicz projection inequalities, not these claims. Dedicated semantic mathematical literature comparisons did not reveal stronger coverage; these searches do not prove historical novelty.
residual_risks: The scalar perspective inequality is explicitly known in 2010 and can make the weak form of interpolation routine; the proposed novelty is its strict global body-level equality rigidity and exact positive-definite translation Hessian for the 2026 critical family.

value.rationale: This theorem gives a natural complete structural answer to how the freshly introduced origin-dependent critical smooth-covariogram body changes as one moves the reference origin. It proves strict set-valued Minkowski interpolation in all dimensions and for every smooth positively curved convex body; this yields strict volume-root concavity and at most one optimal origin. For centrally symmetric bodies, it identifies the unique optimal center at every positive critical level, establishes strict radial shrinkage, and computes an explicit positive-definite Hessian integral governing local volume stability. The result is neither a table recomputation nor an arbitrary special slice; the disk quadrature only illustrates the general theorem.
